purpose: Anchor readings enrich Units 1–11 through Read & Notice, Math Connection, and Evidence & Synthesis. Required reading intentionally ends after Unit 11 so students can focus on design, cumulative capstone evidence, and the separate final examination.
calendar_note: The live course is 36 weeks with mixed unit lengths. Unit 12 is a reading intermission during CAD/design work. Unit 13 contains no new lessons and no required reading.
mastery_policy: Reading activities enrich geometry, vocabulary, evidence use, and critical thinking but do not replace the 80% mathematics mastery gate.
source_policy: Prefer public-domain, openly licensed, or legitimately free-access sources. Preserve attribution and provide accessible excerpts/reading guides.

required_reading_units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
required_reading_units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
required_reading_units.critical_question: What must be accepted, defined, constructed, or proved before a geometric conclusion is trustworthy?

required_reading_units.anchor: Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions
required_reading_units.author: Edwin A. Abbott
required_reading_units.critical_question: Which properties belong to a figure itself, and which depend on the observer or representation?

required_reading_units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid — Book I congruence selections
required_reading_units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
required_reading_units.critical_question: How much information is sufficient to force two triangles to agree?

required_reading_units.author: David Hilbert
required_reading_units.critical_question: Which facts about lines follow from definitions and axioms, and which require additional evidence?

required_reading_units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid — Book VI
required_reading_units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
required_reading_units.critical_question: What must remain proportional for a scale model to represent the original faithfully?

required_reading_units.author: Harold Jacoby
required_reading_units.critical_question: How can angle and direction measurements determine a position or distance that cannot be measured directly?

required_reading_units.anchor: Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions — polygon selections
required_reading_units.author: Edwin A. Abbott
required_reading_units.critical_question: When does a classification follow from geometric properties, and when is it merely an imposed label?

required_reading_units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid — Book III
required_reading_units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
required_reading_units.critical_question: Which circle relationships are consequences of radius and symmetry rather than visual appearance?

required_reading_units.author: W. H. Besant
required_reading_units.critical_question: How can one geometric condition generate an entire curve?

required_reading_units.author: John Venn
required_reading_units.critical_question: When does a measured or observed frequency justify a probability claim, and what uncertainty remains?

required_reading_units.anchor: Solid Geometry with Problems and Applications
required_reading_units.author: H. E. Slaught and N. J. Lennes
required_reading_units.critical_question: Why do length, area, and volume scale differently when a solid is enlarged?

fadeout.reason: Students focus on CAD, scale drawing, spatial design, applied portfolio work, and mathematical production. No assigned anchor reading.

No new lessons and no assigned reading. Students complete a separate 50-question cumulative capstone covering Units 1–12, corrections, completion evidence, and then the independent comprehensive final examination.
